evals.prompt: We adopted the Agentic SDLC last month. Our repo is on GitHub with one workflow running npm test. Set up the CI gates and branch protection so approvals are actually enforced.
evals.expected_output: Setup mode: discovery report of existing CI, DoD mapping with drift findings, installation of the agentic-sdlc workflow and CODEOWNERS through a plan task and PR, proposed branch protection and production environment settings awaiting the admin's explicit yes, and a gate-proof plan
expectations: Output inspects the existing workflow, the sdlc-dod block and current protection read-only before proposing changes, and maps each DoD key to a CI job (identical, drift, missing, n/a)
Output installs the agentic-sdlc workflow and CODEOWNERS via a plan task and pull request rather than committing them directly to the default branch

Output proposes required checks agentic-sdlc/dod, spec and approvals with strict mode, dismiss stale reviews, code owner review, enforce admins and no force pushes, and does not require agentic-sdlc/trace while trace-check is not vendored
Output configures or proposes a production environment whose required reviewers are the Release Owner(s) with self-review prevented
Output shows the exact settings commands and asks the repository admin for an explicit yes, ending the turn before changing settings
Output keeps Enforcement prompt-only until every gate has been proven to block a bad change

evals.prompt: The checks are green on the workflow file and branch protection is on. Just mark enforcement as branch-protection, we don't have time to open fake PRs.
evals.expected_output: Refusal to set the Enforcement line without proof, with a short proof plan (violation, clean control, tool error, host-control cases) and the evidence row format
expectations: Output does not set Enforcement to branch-protection without recorded proof that each required gate blocked a bad change
Output proposes concrete proof cases such as a spec edited after approval (AP04), a failing test, a coverage drop and a stale-review push, each on a gate-proof branch as a draft PR
Output reads the merge state with gh pr view rather than attempting to merge the bad change
Output records evidence rows with IDs like Gate:<name>:<case>, observed output, merge state, link, date and author
Output uses an independent pass (or labels self-review) to design violations that might still pass

evals.prompt: Stage 1 of the CSV export rollout has been live 30 minutes on internal users. Baseline error rate 0.42%, p95 310 ms. Current: 58 requests, 0% errors, p95 290 ms, alert silent. PM says it's clean, go to 10% now.
evals.expected_output: Hold decision because the event count is below 100, with the arithmetic, a hold row in the deploy log, and the rule for extending to at most 2x the stage minimum
expectations: Output decides HOLD, not advance, because 58 requests is below the 100-event minimum
Output shows the limits 0.92% error rate and 341 ms p95 computed from the baseline
Output writes a deploy log row with decision 'hold — <reason>'
Output states that at 2 x the stage minimum (60 min) still undecided the Release Owner chooses roll back by default or stay with a recorded reason
Output does not lower or skip a threshold because of time pressure from the PM

evals.prompt: Stage 2 at 10% after 60 minutes: error rate 0.95% against baseline 0.42%, p95 330 ms, alert silent, no incidents. It's barely over, let's hold another hour and see if it settles.
evals.expected_output: Immediate roll back: run the approved rollback and verify commands, log them, open an incident at SEV2 or higher, hand to the SRE, stop; re-release needs a new go/no-go and Release sign-off
expectations: Output decides ROLL BACK because 0.95% exceeds the 0.92% limit, and refuses to use hold to wait out a breach
Output runs only the rollback and verify commands named in the approved release notes and records both outputs in the deploy log
Output opens an incident at SEV2 or higher and hands over to the SRE (operations-and-incidents)
Output states that a re-release needs a new go/no-go and a new Release sign-off

evals.prompt: We have no staging environment. Rehearse the rollback for the flag reports.csvExport so we can release today.
evals.expected_output: R3 and R5 reported as CANNOT_VERIFY, release only under an accept-risk waiver signed by the Release Owner (owner not the requester, expiry at most 30 days, follow-up issue), no rehearsal faked in production
expectations: Output marks R3 (rollback rehearsal) and R5 (test alert) as CANNOT_VERIFY instead of claiming them
Output requires an accept-risk waiver with owner different from the requester, expiry at most 30 days and a follow-up issue to create staging
Output does not run the rollback rehearsal against production as a substitute
Output still records R4 by reading the production flag value as off before stage 1
Output hands the checklist to shipping-and-handover for the go/no-go and Release sign-off request
